mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the scientific study of the sound system of a language."
Phonology is the scientific study of the sound system of a language.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the upper and lower jaws, which come together in the formation or articulation of the speech sounds."
Housed by these organs are the upper and lower jaws, which come together in the formation or articulation of the speech sounds.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the insertion of a vowel between a consonant clusters."
More common in English language is the insertion of a vowel between a consonant clusters.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a function of the connected speech or what we regard as the colloquial speech."
Assimilation process is a function of the connected speech or what we regard as the colloquial speech.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an arrangement of symbols or numbers in columns and rows in order to describe or express a set of given information."
A matrix is an arrangement of symbols or numbers in columns and rows in order to describe or express a set of given information.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is defined as phonemes that never occur in the same environment."
Complementary distribution is defined as phonemes that never occur in the same environment.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the feature used to describe the sounds that are produced with the flat part of the tongue called the blade."
Coronal is the feature used to describe the sounds that are produced with the flat part of the tongue called the blade.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a feature of mainly the nose as this is the chamber or cavity which a nasal sound undergoes during production."
Nasality is a feature of mainly the nose as this is the chamber or cavity which a nasal sound undergoes during production.
fib: ______ is defined as the rise and fall of the pitch of an utterance (Jolayemi, 1999: 82).
Intonation
Intonation is defined as the rise and fall of the pitch of an utterance (Jolayemi, 1999: 82).
______ is the smallest/indivisible and contrastive or significant unit of the sound of a language, which, when replaced with another sound, results in a change in meaning.
phoneme
A phoneme is the smallest/indivisible and contrastive or significant unit of the sound of a language, which, when replaced with another sound, results in a change in meaning.
______ are the lips, teeth, teeth ridge, tongue, pharynx, and even the nose, etc.
Major among these organs
Major among these organs are the lips, teeth, teeth ridge, tongue, pharynx, and even the nose, etc.
______ is the main organ of the ear that connects the rest of the ear to the brain where the operations on speech reception and perception end.
inner ear
The inner ear is the main organ of the ear that connects the rest of the ear to the brain where the operations on speech reception and perception end.
______ is a term used to describe the activities that take place when the vocal folds are shut and there are continuous vibrations at the larynx.
Sonorant
Sonorant is a term used to describe the activities that take place when the vocal folds are shut and there are continuous vibrations at the larynx.
______ is the EXTERNAL manifestation of the INTERNALLY encased UR, which enables the owner of the language to express what he has in his mind to say for the hearer to hear.
Phonetic representation
Phonetic representation is the EXTERNAL manifestation of the INTERNALLY encased UR, which enables the owner of the language to express what he has in his mind to say for the hearer to hear.
______ is described as a flat shape of four corners that has four straight lines, two of which are of equal length.
trapezium (trapezoid in American English)
trapezium
A trapezium (trapezoid in American English) is described as a flat shape of four corners that has four straight lines, two of which are of equal length.
